standard_prerequisites.name: The maximal submodule supported in closed points
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1289-1297: the maximal coherent submodule I of O_X supported in closed points exists, and its vanishing is equivalent to X having no embedded points.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaves with zero-dimensional support are globally generated
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1291-1293: I is globally generated; since 1 in Gamma(X, O_X) is not a section of I, one gets I = 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: No embedded points gives Serre's S1
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1297-1299: X has (S_1) because it has no embedded points, hence is Cohen-Macaulay in dimension 1.

core_obligations: Connectedness and equidimensionality (proof lines 1283-1288): Gamma(X, O_X) = k has no nontrivial idempotents, so X is connected; this already shows X is equidimensional of dimension 1, since any irreducible component of dimension 0 would be a connected component.

Killing embedded points (lines 1289-1297): let I be the maximal coherent submodule supported in closed points; it exists (divisors-lemma-remove-embedded-points) and is globally generated (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite); since 1 in Gamma(X, O_X) is not a section of I, one concludes I = 0, and thus X has no embedded points.
Cohen-Macaulay conclusion (lines 1297-1301): by divisors-lemma-S1-no-embedded the absence of embedded points gives (S_1), and a 1-dimensional (S_1) scheme is Cohen-Macaulay.
proof_roadmap: Get connectedness from the idempotent-free ring of global functions and equidimensionality from connectedness.
Show the maximal closed-point-supported submodule vanishes using global generation and the section 1.
difficulty_reason: Structural lemma (statement 1276-1281, proof 1283-1301): a proper 1-dimensional k-scheme with H^0(O_X) = k is automatically connected, Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional - the proof chains idempotents, the maximal submodule supported in closed points, global generation and Serre's condition; every step is justified by a cited lemma and no verification is omitted. H2: short chain of standard arguments.
